metadata.headline: How does Farfetch make 1,400 luxury partners feel like one store?

platform_lesson.title: The inventory can stay fragmented while the customer experience is unified
platform_lesson.text: Farfetch's core marketplace does not need to own the luxury inventory it sells. Brands and boutiques keep the stock, while Farfetch turns thousands of separate inventories into one searchable checkout and customer experience. That makes cross-border logistics structurally important: after a customer buys from one or several partners, the physical products still have to move from those distributed inventories to a customer who may be in another country. Farfetch therefore orchestrates discovery, payment, partner settlement, shipping options, tracking and returns around inventory it does not hold. The platform lesson is that aggregation can centralize the customer experience without centralizing the underlying assets.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Luxury Listing is the Core Value Unit: a specific luxury item from a brand or boutique, represented with product, price, size and availability information so it can be discovered and purchased globally through Farfetch.

actor.explanation: Luxury Customers use Farfetch to discover and buy products from brands and boutiques around the world through one interface.

metrics.note: Farfetch's current company page describes its customer base as millions of active customers. No precise current active-customer count is publicly disclosed.

job.explanation: Customers want to find desirable luxury products, including pieces that may not be available in their local market.

gain.explanation: Farfetch combines fragmented global inventory into a broad selection with one discovery and checkout experience.

pain.explanation: Luxury e-commerce creates friction around price, fit, customs, returns, delivery time and cross-border complexity.

transaction.explanation: Customers place orders and pay through Farfetch even when the underlying sale is with a third-party partner boutique.

filter.explanation: Access and availability depend on destination market, payment eligibility, shipping restrictions and partner inventory.

access_channel.explanation: Customers access the marketplace through Farfetch's website and mobile applications.

activities.explanation: Customers browse, compare, purchase and return luxury products.

resources.explanation: Customers contribute purchasing power, style preferences, sizing information and shopping behavior.

actor.explanation: Independent luxury brands, boutiques and department stores provide the distributed inventory that Farfetch aggregates.

metrics.note: Farfetch currently states that it connects customers with items from more than 1,400 brands and boutiques worldwide.

job.explanation: Providers want to reach international luxury customers without building the same global digital demand and transaction layer themselves.

gain.explanation: Farfetch provides international discovery, demand generation and access to markets beyond the Provider's local footprint.

pain.explanation: Providers must keep inventory, pricing and product information accurate while fulfilling premium cross-border orders.

transaction.explanation: Providers supply product listings, availability and the physical inventory behind them.

filter.explanation: Farfetch controls which retail partners join and applies marketplace, product, service and content requirements.

access_channel.explanation: Brands and boutiques connect their catalog, stock and order-management processes to Farfetch's partner systems.

activities.explanation: Providers maintain product data and stock, prepare sold items and hand parcels into the delivery network.

resources.explanation: Providers contribute luxury inventory, product data, pricing, brand identity and fulfillment capability.

actor.explanation: Logistics Carriers are the most business-model-critical external complement in the global marketplace boundary. Farfetch currently ships worldwide primarily through DHL, with UPS and other carriers used in selected markets, so distributed boutique inventory can reach customers without Farfetch owning the stock.

job.explanation: Carriers must move high-value products reliably across the local and international routes connecting Farfetch partners with customers.

gain.explanation: Farfetch creates recurring premium parcel volume across many countries and retail origins.

pain.explanation: Cross-border luxury shipments face customs, security, delivery-time and loss or damage risk.

transaction.explanation: Providers hand parcels to the carrier network; carriers move them to customers and support the reverse flow for returns.

filter.explanation: The carrier layer needs international coverage, tracking and service levels compatible with a premium luxury experience.

access_channel.explanation: Farfetch integrates shipping options, labels and tracking into the order and return process.

activities.explanation: Carriers collect or receive parcels, transport them, clear relevant delivery steps and complete delivery.

resources.explanation: Carriers contribute global parcel networks, customs capability, tracking systems and delivery capacity.

actor.explanation: Farfetch operates the luxury marketplace and customer interface. Coupang acquired the Farfetch business and assets in January 2024.

metrics.note: Farfetch currently serves customers in more than 190 countries and territories. This is geographic marketplace reach, not a revenue or customer-count metric.

job.explanation: Farfetch turns fragmented global luxury inventory into one searchable and transactional destination.

gain.explanation: Aggregated demand and supply can increase marketplace liquidity and generate transaction-related economics.

pain.explanation: Farfetch must coordinate premium service, partner economics, global fulfillment and profitability across a fragmented supply base.

transaction.explanation: Farfetch coordinates discovery, ordering, customer payment and commercial settlement with the selling partner.

governance.explanation: Farfetch governs retail-partner eligibility, listing quality, customer service, returns and marketplace standards.

promotion_channel.explanation: Farfetch attracts luxury demand through campaigns, search, editorial merchandising, exclusives and brand storytelling.

activities.explanation: Farfetch operates discovery, checkout, partner integration, customer support, settlement and shipping orchestration.

resources.explanation: Its global retail network, customer base, fashion data and marketplace technology are strategic resources.

current.explanation: Customers place orders and payment through Farfetch's unified checkout.
Farfetch provides global discovery, checkout, customer support, shipping coordination and returns.
Brands and boutiques provide product listings, inventory availability and commercial data.
Farfetch routes customer demand to the selling partner and remits the relevant proceeds after the transaction.
The underlying purchase contract is with the partner boutique or brand, so the customer's order creates direct demand for that Provider's product.
The selling partner supplies the purchased item, which is shipped from that partner's inventory to the customer.
The logistics carrier physically delivers the purchased product to the customer.
The selling brand or boutique hands the packed order into the carrier network.
The carrier provides transport and tracking that allow the Provider to fulfill the Farfetch order.
Farfetch orchestrates shipping options and creates parcel volume across its distributed retail network.
Carrier status and delivery events feed Farfetch's customer-service, tracking and return processes.

metrics.note: Current Farfetch geographic reach across countries and territories.
Current qualitative active-customer scale statement; no precise count disclosed.
Current Farfetch global brand-and-boutique partner count.

sources.title: Cases only.pptx — Farfetch source case
sources.note: Internal source reconstruction used only as a starting point. It identified Farfetch, luxury customers, brands/boutiques, a broad commerce-services Partner set and a luxury fashion listing as the original CVU.

sources.title: What is FARFETCH?
sources.note: Primary source for the current marketplace model, 1,400+ global brand/boutique partners, 190+ countries and territories and millions of active customers.

sources.title: Farfetch Terms and Conditions
sources.note: Primary legal source confirming that customers generally buy from third-party partner boutiques, Farfetch collects payment and remits proceeds, Farfetch provides shipping services, and items ship directly from partner inventory.

sources.title: How to shop on FARFETCH
sources.note: Primary source for one-checkout aggregation across multiple retail partners and worldwide shipping via DHL, with UPS in selected countries.

sources.title: Orders & Shipping
sources.note: Primary source for direct partner-origin shipments, separate packages by boutique, shipping/tracking and the carrier network including DHL, UPS, FedEx, TNT and DPD.

sources.title: FARFETCH FIRST
sources.note: Primary current source showing how delivery speed has become part of Farfetch's premium customer proposition, with next-day delivery across Europe for selected inventory.

sources.title: Coupang 2025 Form 10-K
sources.note: Primary filing confirming Coupang's January 2024 acquisition of Farfetch and describing the Farfetch marketplace as connecting luxury sellers with customers.

sources.title: FARFETCH opens a world of luxury to millions of new and engaged customers
sources.note: Current strategic context for R.LUX integration. Used to show why R.LUX is a regional growth channel inside the Coupang group rather than the core global Partner role.
